newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, 30-yr yield at new low.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, 30-yr yield at new low.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in heavy trading on Wednesday, with sharp gains in U.S. treasuries and a stronger Canadian dollar helping send prices higher, analysts said.

"Obviously both North American bond markets have just had an incredible rally here. It's getting harder and harder just to see how much more they can go over the near term," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.08 to C$122.31 to yield 6.326 percent, a record low yield for the 30-year benchmark bonds.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 23/32 to yield 6.34 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to negative one basis point from a positive spread of two basis points at Tuesday's close.
Analysts said the impetus for the rise in Canada came from the United States, where retail, hedge fund and central bank buying brought the 30-year bond yield to its lowest in a year and a half.

The Canadian bond market outperformed partly because of a stronger currency, dealers said. Canada's dollar closed stronger in heavy trading on buying linked to the expiry of options, and foreign buying of Canadian equities.
Looking ahead, bond investors are now awaiting U.S. non-farm payrolls data for July on Friday and U.S. GDP data on Thursday.
The Government of Canada on Thursday will also release details of its 10-year bond auction on August 6.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.56 to C$110.68 to yield 5.806 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.05 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 24 basis points from 23 basis points at Tuesday's close.
